text: What is meant by a volatile liquid?
options: A liquid that does not evaporate
A liquid that reacts violently with water
A liquid with a very high boiling point
A liquid that evaporates easily and has a high vapour pressure
explanation: Volatility describes how readily a liquid vaporises. Weak intermolecular forces give a high saturated vapour pressure and a low boiling point.

text: Which of the following statements about vapour pressure are correct? I. Vapour pressure decreases as temperature increases II. Adding a non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure of a liquid III. Saturated vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid
explanation:

text: Why does water boil below 100°C on a high mountain?
options: Water is purer at high altitude
The air is colder at high altitude
Atmospheric pressure is lower, so the vapour pressure equals it at a lower temperature
Water has a higher vapour pressure at altitude
explanation: Boiling occurs when saturated vapour pressure equals external pressure. Less atmospheric pressure means that condition is met at a lower temperature.
